title: A plan step that tells the phase executor to dispatch is unexecutable by construction — catch it at authoring time (gh-428)
body:
Closes #428 (items 1, 2 and 4).

A plan step can tell `fr-phase-executor` to dispatch a subagent. Its tool grant has no `Agent` (OpenCode: `task: deny`), so it is a leaf and can never dispatch anything. It does the nearest thing it can, reports the deviation honestly — **and ticks the step anyway**. The plan then records completion for work nobody performed. No tool call is ever made, which is why #422's PreToolUse hook is structurally blind to it and why this lands at authoring time instead.

- **Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-agentic-dispatch-verb-lint-design.md`
- **Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-agentic-dispatch-verb-lint/`

## Rebased onto 4.12.0 — and two concepts moved

This branch was opened against 4.8.1. Main has since shipped seven commits to
**4.12.0**, including the run-schema 4→5 rewrite, and *two of them moved
concepts this design depends on*. Both are addressed here, not papered over:

**The escape route is narrower than the spec recorded.** #496 shipped
`_manual_placement_issues`: no manual phase may be *outstanding* when an agentic
phase after it runs. So this lint's advice — "move the dispatch into a
`[manual]` phase" — now hands the author a plan that fails the sibling gate.
Demonstrated on the merged code with three plans: the dispatch step errors with
#428; making that phase manual *mid-plan* swaps it for #496's placement error;
only the **trailing** manual phase is clean. The message, the fr-plan bullet and
the CLI test all say `TRAILING` now, and the test pins **both** issue numbers so
the two gates cannot drift back into contradicting each other.

**#428 item 3 has shipped — do not file it.** Decision d1 deferred it as "a new
CLI surface, its own issue". gh-503 built it more generally while this branch
was in flight: `UnitRecord.evidence` maps an obligation to a journal entry id
verified when the unit resolves, `_VERIFIABLE_EVIDENCE = ("review", "findings")`
is the closed vocabulary (with `findings` *derived*, so it cannot be satisfied
by typing a flag), and the shipped `fr-goal.yaml` declares
`evidence: [review, findings]` on `review-phase`. A completed phase with no
review journal entry cannot resolve — exactly item 3's ask.

Also merged: the executor file gained main's `## Contract` section, so it now
carries two contract-like blocks; a lead line states the difference (the two
refusals are what you *are*, settled before you start; the Contract is how you
work). Run cursor migrated to schema 5. Version re-bumped to **4.13.0**.

**All four previously-red tests are now green** — main fixed every one, and the
two findings they belonged to are resolved in the journal with that attribution.

## What ships

**1. The lint** (`fr plan self-review`, error severity, agentic phases only). Two patterns, both requiring an *instruction boundary*: start-of-text, real punctuation, or a list marker — **never a bare newline**.
- imperative dispatch verb (`dispatch`/`delegate to`/`spawn`/`hand off to`/`fan out to`) with an agent-shaped object within ~60 same-sentence characters;
- mechanism tokens in an instructional frame (`use`/`call`/`invoke` + `the <X> agent`/`subagent`/`Task tool`/`Agent tool`).

Fenced ``` blocks are stripped before scanning; **inline backticks are not** — the backticked agent name *is* the object, and stripping it blinds the detector on the one case it exists for.

**2. The executor contract** (`fr-phase-executor.md`, `fr-execute/SKILL.md`): a dispatch step is a BLOCKER — report it, leave the step **unticked**, do not complete the phase, and do not do the work inline as a substitute. The agent file now states *one* policy ("you are a leaf, on a shared branch") with #420 and #428 as its two refusals, rather than two bolted-on prohibitions.

**3. fr-plan guidance**: steps name outcomes, not mechanisms.

Plus: `rich.markup.escape` in `plan_cmd.py` — see below. Version `4.8.1 → 4.9.0` (minor: a plan that passed on 4.8.x can fail on 4.9.0).

## Precision — the number that shaped the design

#428's literal pattern list, measured over this repo's own plans: **237 false positives on bare `dispatch` alone, 16.7% of agentic steps**, plus 42 on bare `<word>:<word>` tokens (`start:end`, `cli:app`, `fr:synced`). super-fr is a repo *about* dispatch, so at error severity the gate would have been switched off within a week.

The shipped patterns score **0 hits across all 2,113 agentic steps of all 82 plan folders — ticked or not** — while catching 10 of 10 curated true positives, including the observed defect verbatim (``Dispatch `blog-craft:post-researcher` per post``). Pinned by two corpus tests: one gate-accurate, one with every exemption disabled. **15 of 15 mutants die.**

Each refinement is individually justified by counterfactual, not taste:

| revert this | hits reappear |
|---|---|
| newline is not a boundary | 2 — both this plan *describing* the contract |
| instructional frame on mechanism tokens | 2 — both this plan quoting the verdict |
| trailing `\b` on the verb stem | `dispatching` matches via its prefix; the mood rule buys nothing |
| frameless `subagent_type[:=]` | 1 — a legitimate merged plan |
| keep inline backticks | the observed defect stops matching entirely |

## Findings — 19 fixed, 4 open

Eight review rounds across four phases. The ones that changed the design:

- **Half the detector was deletable with the suite green.** Replacing `_RE_DISPATCH_MECHANISM` with a never-matching regex left 85/85 passing — pattern 2 had no true-positive test. The plan asked for "the six observed shapes" and all six were pattern-1 shapes.
- **A false claim in shipped source.** The comment said "ZERO over 2,113 steps" while pattern 2 had a live hit in a plan merged three days earlier — invisible because the corpus test only saw what the *gate* sees, and the gate exempts ticked steps (87% of the corpus). Fixed structurally: a second corpus test now scans every step with no exemptions.
- **A soft line-wrap faked an instruction boundary**, flagging this plan's own prose. Plan text is hard-wrapped everywhere, so this would have fired on ordinary sentences forever.
- **Fence stripping mis-paired 4-backtick fences** and thereby *un-fenced* the quoted instruction it exists to protect — the exact shape phases 3 and 4 needed.
- **`rich` ate every bracketed token** in `fr plan self-review` output. The new verdict rendered as *"or move the dispatch into a  phase"*, with the escape route deleted, and every issue the command has ever printed lost its `[error]`/`[warn]` prefix the same way.
- **A test that named more than it asserted.** `test_..._names_both_escapes` asserted one; deleting "Name the OUTCOME instead" from the message left it green — the half that tells an author what to write instead.
- **A vacuous fixture, caught by mutation**: the first fence test passed with `_strip_fenced_code` deleted.
- **A fabricated test name passed every gate in the repo.** `fr acceptance check` validates `--level` refs but never reads prose notes, so an invented name in a `notes` field is invisible to CI. Caught by grep. A second instance in the same phase put a *false explanation* of the corpus delta into three committed reports.
- **This PR staled a code citation inside the paragraph it edited** — inserting the detector moved `self_review` from :876 to :1079, and the explainer still pointed at the old range.

## Operator gates

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

One touchpoint, as designed: the batched Q&A. Decisions recorded in `docs/superpowers/journals/specs/2026-09-20-agentic-dispatch-verb-lint.md` — scope (items 1/2/4; item 3 and #496 excluded), precision-first with a single error tier, `[manual]` phase as the only escape, and the model-tier bindings.

## Acceptance

Rows added since `origin/main` (born at brainstorm, presented then):

| row | status | defense |
|---|---|---|
| `goal-agentic-dispatch-purity` | **ci** | The business claim: authoring a dispatch step into an agentic phase fails, naming both escapes. Unit-pinned end to end including the CLI exit code. |
| `goal-dispatch-lint-precision` | **ci** | The claim that makes the gate usable in a repo about dispatch — zero errors on every plan already written. Without it the lint is one widening away from being disabled. |
| `goal-executor-refuses-tick` | **skipped** | Deliberately **not** `ci`. The token tests pin the contract is *present*, not *obeyed*; the behaviour is agent-side and not unit-testable, and on Hermes the prose is the whole enforcement. Backfill owed: a live executor run against a pre-lint dispatch step. |

Debt overall: `ci: 107, skipped: 19, not-implemented: 4` (130 rows). No row moved that this PR did not earn.

## Test Plan

**No post-merge Test Plan is owed** — this ships a lint and prose; nothing deploys. Verification is unit-level and in CI: **4,010 passed, 0 failed**, coverage 92.30%.

## Open findings — two, each needing its own issue

1. **~44 unescaped rich interpolations** under `packages/fr/src/fr/commands/`.
   `[manual]`-shaped tokens are silently dropped and a `[/red]`-shaped one
   raises `MarkupError` — so `fr plan self-review` can crash on the parse error
   it exists to report. Only the one site this PR depends on is fixed.
2. **`fr status` says "merged but not archived"** for any locally-complete plan
   and recommends `fr archive --all`. The check is deliberately gh-free; the
   label asserts a merge it never observed. Every fr-goal run reaches this state
   *before* its PR exists, so the suggestion fires exactly when archiving would
   be wrong, and `implemented/` is frozen. (Contrast
   `test_no_merged_but_unarchived_plans`, which consults `origin/main` first —
   the well-built version of the same signal.)

Two earlier findings were **resolved by main**, not by this branch: the three
host-dependent red tests, and the unarchived-plan tripwire (#512).

A third is recorded but deliberately not fixed: the explainer's line-range
citations went stale **twice** in this PR — once when the detector was inserted,
once when the merge moved `self_review` again. They are a cross-file invariant
with no guard (`test_tripwire_explainers_fresh.py` checks only title and
headings, as the rule's own Known gaps admit). Closing it means either citing
symbols or resolving each range at test time.

## Ready-checklist guard — do not merge until all three hold

- [x] CI green (**local full suite: 4,010 passed, 0 failed**)
- [x] explicit review ok
- [x] no commits since that ok
